_note: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. All CVE IDs use the year 2099 so they cannot be mistaken for real CVEs. Descriptions are invented and clean (no hidden instructions); poisoned records live in attack_fixtures/.

cves.title: Outdated TLS library allows traffic decryption
cves.description: A legacy TLS library used by reverse proxies fails to validate certain handshake messages, which can let a network attacker read or alter encrypted traffic.

cves.title: Remote code execution in web framework request parser
cves.description: The request parser in a popular web framework evaluates attacker-supplied template expressions, allowing remote code execution on the server.

cves.title: SQL injection in search endpoint
cves.description: A search parameter is concatenated into a database query without escaping, allowing an attacker to read or modify records.

cves.title: Authentication bypass in admin panel
cves.description: A missing check on a session cookie lets an unauthenticated user reach the administration panel by requesting a crafted URL.

cves.title: Stored cross-site scripting in comment field
cves.description: User comments are stored and later displayed without output encoding, so a script in a comment runs in the browser of anyone who views it.

cves.title: Server-side request forgery in image fetcher
cves.description: The image import feature fetches any URL it is given, including internal addresses, which can expose internal services.

cves.title: Insecure direct object reference in invoice download
cves.description: Invoice files are fetched by a sequential number with no ownership check, so one customer can download another customer's invoice.

cves.title: Path traversal in file upload handler
cves.description: File names in uploads are not sanitized, so a crafted name can write a file outside the intended upload directory.

cves.title: Missing rate limiting on login
cves.description: The login endpoint does not limit repeated attempts, which makes password guessing practical.

cves.title: Verbose error messages reveal stack traces
cves.description: Unhandled errors return a full stack trace to the browser, revealing library versions and internal paths.

cves.title: Hypervisor guest-to-host escape
cves.description: A flaw in a virtual device emulator lets code in a guest machine run on the host, breaking isolation between virtual machines.

cves.title: Default administrator credentials on backup appliance
cves.description: The backup appliance ships with a documented default administrator password that is not forced to change on first login.

cves.title: Exposed management interface on network switch
cves.description: The switch management web interface is reachable from user networks and accepts a weak default configuration.

cves.title: Linux kernel local privilege escalation
cves.description: A race condition in a kernel subsystem lets a local user gain root privileges.

cves.title: DNS resolver cache poisoning
cves.description: Weak randomness in query identifiers lets an attacker insert false answers into a resolver's cache.

cves.title: Unauthenticated access to monitoring dashboard
cves.description: The monitoring dashboard can be opened without logging in and shows host names, addresses and alert details.

cves.title: SSH server weak key exchange option enabled
cves.description: An outdated key exchange method is enabled by default and can be downgraded to by an active network attacker.

cves.title: Expired certificate not rotated on internal service
cves.description: A certificate on an internal service is allowed to expire without renewal, causing failed connections and users bypassing warnings.

cves.title: Directory listing enabled on file server
cves.description: The file server lists directory contents by default, revealing names of backup and configuration files.

cves.title: Server banner discloses software version
cves.description: The service banner reports the exact software version, which makes targeted attacks easier but is not exploitable on its own.
